title: Streams API
objectives: Build pipelines with intermediate and terminal operations
Use collectors and know when parallel streams help

sections.markdown: The Streams API (Java 8) processes sequences of elements declaratively through a pipeline of operations — filter, map, reduce — instead of explicit loops.

sections.code:
List<String> names = people.stream()      // source
    .filter(p -> p.age() >= 18)            // intermediate (lazy)
    .map(Person::name)                     // intermediate (lazy)
    .sorted()
    .collect(Collectors.toList());         // terminal (triggers run)

sections.markdown: Streams are **lazy**: intermediate ops don't run until a terminal op is called, enabling fusion and short-circuiting (e.g., findFirst stops at the first match).
Reusing a consumed stream (IllegalStateException) or using parallel streams blindly — they add overhead and can be slower for small or I/O-bound data, and break with shared mutable state.

flashcards.back: Intermediate ops are lazy and return a stream (filter/map); terminal ops trigger execution and return a result (collect/reduce).
Laziness + operation fusion + short-circuiting — work happens only when a terminal op runs, and can stop early.
Small datasets, I/O-bound work, or shared mutable state — overhead and correctness issues.
